hint.text: Geothermal refers to the heat that comes from beneath the Earth’s surface.
hint.label: Geothermal

atoms.a: Iceland has a lot of geothermal activity and more active volcanoes than anywhere else in Europe.
In south-western Iceland, you can find many geysers, which are hot springs that erupt steam and boiling water.
atoms.sound: In south-western Iceland, you can find many geezers, which are hot springs that erupt steam and boiling water.

atoms.a: 90% of all homes in Iceland are heated by geothermal energy, which is a renewable energy source.
Geothermal spas attract more than half of Iceland’s tourists annually.

atoms.b: The Øresund Bridge ((++connects disconnects)) Copenhagen, the capital of Denmark, to the city of Malmö in Sweden.
atoms.sound: The Øresund Bridge connects Copenhaygan, the capital of Denmark, to the city of Malmö in Sweden.

atoms.b: Northern Europe has countless ((++islands trees)). In fact, Sweden, Finland and Norway are the three countries with the most islands in the world.

hint.label: Island rankings
hint.text:
These are the five countries with the most islands in the world:

1. Sweden 267,500 islands
2. Finland 239,000 islands
3. Norway 179,000 islands
4. Canada 52,500 islands
5. Japan 14,000 islands
hint.sound: These are the five countries with the most islands in the world.

atoms.b: Many of these islands are uninhabited due to their isolated locations and extreme ((++polar tropical)) climate.

trainers.instruction: Lots of interesting things happen in the skies of the Arctic Circle. Listen and select the correct definition.

b.sound: Colourful lights in the night sky of the Arctic Circle.
Colourful clouds that can only be seen on a clear day in Antarctica.
In the summer months, the sun never sets and, in winter, there is total darkness for weeks at a time.
In both the summer and winter months the sun never rises.

text.text: As the Earth orbits the Sun, the North Pole tilts towards the Sun in summer and away from it in winter. Parts of Europe are so far north that this has a major effect on their daylight hours.

trainers.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: For thousands of years, the entirety of Northern Europe was covered in slow-moving masses of ice called glaciers. As they moved, they carved out the land beneath them. Over time, the glaciers melted, revealing unique landscapes such as lake districts and fjords.
Finland has the largest lake district in Europe and is known as the Land of a Thousand Lakes. There are over 55,000 lakes spread across the nation.
Norway has many fjords that make up its long, winding coastline. Fjords are large inlets of sea with steep cliffs on either side. Each year, Norway’s fjords attract hundreds of thousands of tourists.

atoms.a: What has shaped the landscape of Northern Europe?
How many lakes are in Finland?

b: ++a large inlet of sea with steep cliffs
